Rules / Modernization

SK1010 Use is null / is not null instead of == / !=

A null comparison written with an operator, on a type that does not define one.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 9.0
Since0.6

Why

x == null calls whatever operator == the type declares; x is null is a pattern and always tests reference (or default) equality. On a type with a user-defined == the two are different programs, and on a type without one they are the same program written two ways. Preferring the pattern removes the question. It also survives a later refactor that adds an operator ==, which is exactly when == null silently changes meaning.

Example

Instead of:

if (source != null) {
    Use(source);
}

Write:

if (source is not null) {
    Use(source);
}

The ReSharper mapping

⚠ A choice, not a derivation. The author's export carries at least six inspections over this ground at four severities: merge_into_pattern (suggestion), arrange_null_checking_pattern (hint), convert_type_check_to_null_check (warning), convert_type_check_pattern_to_null_check (warning), join_null_check_with_usage (suggestion), use_null_propagation (hint). MergeIntoPattern is the closest and the mapping is recorded rather than computed. docs/plan/16 § Q5.

When it does not fire

The rule is silent unless the semantic model resolves the non-null operand's type and that type declares no operator ==/operator !=, directly or on any base type. It is silent on unconstrained type parameters (where == null has its own lifted meaning), on dynamic, on pointer types, on any operand whose type could not be resolved, and inside an expression tree, where the pattern form does not compile.
